clue.text: Compile faulty argument

indicators.note: something faulty is badly made, so the letters of the word before it are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together a flawed line of reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges the seven letters of COMPILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a forceful written or spoken attack, a strongly argued case.

clue.text: Mop coat spoilt in river

indicators.note: something spoilt is messed up, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mop and coat ruined in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the river that flows past Washington DC.

clue.text: Picture shows lights on the promontory

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to light on is to land on, so lights means lands
a cape is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A painting shows lamps on a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' looks like lamps but is the verb, as a bird lights (lands) on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting or picture of rural scenery.

clue.text: Detective in scrap throws a left

indicators.note: throwing away a left means removing the letter L, short for left

parts.note: a morsel is a scrap or small piece

explanation.surface: A detective in a fight throws a left hook.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a fictional Oxford detective of novels and British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is a famous fictional detective created by Colin Dexter.

clue.text: Student tucks into excellent pork accompaniment

indicators.note: tucking into something puts it inside, so the student letter goes inside

parts.note: cracking is British slang for excellent
L, for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student eats heartily some fine roast pork side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating but puts L inside CRACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted skin served with roast pork.

clue.text: Some mix in nut and meat product

indicators.note: the first piece is placed inside the nut that follows the word in

parts.note: a pecan is a kind of nut

indicators.note: only some of the word mix is taken, its opening part

explanation.surface: Part of a mixture goes into a nut-and-meat foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes only the opening pair of letters of 'mix'. This single-M spelling is a recognised variant of the more usual double-M form.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is dried pounded meat mixed with fat, a preserved meat product of North American origin.

clue.text: Ruth embraces oriental devotion

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the pity word encloses the eastern letter

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion
E for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth hugs an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name but is the archaic noun for pity (as in ruthless).
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion and reverence.

clue.text: Abigail does without a calculator for a period

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the letter a from the maid word

parts.note: an abigail is a lady's maid, and the 's can stand for does, so this gives maid's
a summer is one who sums, a calculator

explanation.surface: A woman called Abigail manages without a pocket calculator for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abigail' is a dated word for a lady's maid; 's as does gives MAIDS, less A gives MIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer is a period of the year around the summer solstice.

clue.text: Explorer and sailor in bed

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A navigator and a seaman share a bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed to North America for England.

clue.text: Required to restrain a Liberal made angry

indicators.note: restraining someone holds them in, so the required word holds the Liberal letter

parts.note: needed means required
L is short for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: Needing to hold back a politician who was riled.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means irritated or provoked into annoyance.

clue.text: Voice intent

definitions.meaning: a male singing voice pitched above baritone
the general meaning or drift of something said or written

explanation.definitionFit: Tenor names both a high male singing voice and the general purport of a text.

clue.text: Willing to accept daughter can be changed

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so the willing word holds the daughter's letter

parts.note: amenable to something means willing to go along with it
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent may adjust plans if happy to take the daughter in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amendable is open to alteration or correction.

clue.text: Make tyres differently, giving improved access

indicators.note: arranged differently tells us to rearrange the letters of the two words before

explanation.surface: Advice to manufacture tyres in a new way so that cars get better entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key opens many locks, so it grants wider entry than an ordinary key.

clue.text: 'ound the Italian to the point where …

parts.note: the apostrophe drops the H, as in Cockney speech, so 'hound' as a verb, hunt, becomes 'unt
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding hound and an Italian article lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ound tells you to drop the H of the synonym too: hound means hunt, so 'UNT. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time or point at which something happens.

clue.text: … eccentric eats hot vegetable

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the eccentric word swallows the hot letter

parts.note: a card is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric or amusing person
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: An odd fellow munches a spicy vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green vegetable, a variety of beet.

clue.text: Tangle and quarrel with in action

indicators.note: in puts the quarrel and its companion letter inside the action

parts.note: a deed is an action
a rift is a break in relations, a quarrel

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' is not a verb here but the noun for a kind of seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for large brown seaweeds, such as those washed up as driftweed.

clue.text: Is priest getting immoral capital?

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest or monk in Tibet
bad means wicked or immoral

explanation.surface: A question whether a cleric is turning to vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: Immensity of philanthropy shown around the northeast

indicators.note: around says the generosity word goes around the compass letters

parts.note: largess is generous giving, philanthropy
NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: Great charitable giving is seen around the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness is great size, the same as immensity.

clue.text: Carpet the street in blossom

indicators.note: in puts the street inside the blossom

parts.note: bloom means blossom
a road is a street

explanation.surface: Laying down a floor covering in a flowering street.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven on a wide loom.

clue.text: New gaffer initially interrupts foremost film director

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so these letters go inside the word for foremost

parts.note: premier means first or foremost

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of gaffer

explanation.surface: A new boss on set breaks into the work of a leading movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes G from 'gaffer'; with N for 'New' it goes inside PREMIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Preminger was an Austrian-American film director of Anatomy of a Murder and Laura.

clue.text: Rushed Charlie in by lively horse

indicators.note: in puts the rushing and Charlie pieces inside the word for by

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
ran means rushed
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie hurried in, carried by a spirited mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A prancer is a horse that springs and capers, a lively horse.

clue.text: Sailor stays in corrupt place to sleep

indicators.note: staying in something means being inside it, so the sailor goes into the corrupt word

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
OS is short for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman lodges in a crooked dive for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds rest at night, and loosely any place to sleep.

clue.text: Soldier to slip up in bank

indicators.note: in puts the slip inside the bank

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: A soldier makes a blunder at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrier is British slang for a member of the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrier is informal British for a Territorial Army soldier.

clue.text: A king picked up the vernacular

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
got means picked up or acquired

explanation.surface: A monarch learns the local dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is slang or jargon peculiar to a group, its own vernacular speech.

clue.text: Artificial life form discovered by Mongol emperor

indicators.note: discovered by means found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man-made creature unearthed by a Mongol ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered by' picks the run inside 'Mongol emperor'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore a golem is a clay figure brought to life, an artificial being.

clue.text: One makes a claim before getting emotional

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
tender means easily moved or emotional

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a claim before becoming emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is one who claims a title or throne, often without right.

clue.text: Show silver in dish to unbeliever

indicators.note: in puts the silver inside the dish

parts.note: a pan is a shallow dish
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Displaying silver in a dish to a heathen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, one who does not hold the main world religions' beliefs.

clue.text: Invest in experience without resistance

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the resistance letter

parts.note: to endure is to undergo or experience
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Advice to put money into experience while avoiding opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' means to endow or clothe, not to put money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or invest someone with a quality.

clue.text: Associate depression with class

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
a league is a class or level of quality, as in out of one's league

explanation.surface: Linking feeling low with one's place in society.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker, an associate in a profession.

clue.text: Detective recovers stolen loincloth

indicators.note: read as re-covers: the detective word covers the stolen word by enclosing it

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A police officer gets back a stolen piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long loincloth worn by men in India.

clue.text: Rushed round a cross fast

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the others

parts.note: ran means rushed
mad means angry or cross

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted round a crucifix quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a crucifix but means angry; 'fast' is the noun, a period of fasting, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to dusk.

clue.text: Navigate round America in old ship

indicators.note: round says the navigating word goes around the American abbreviation

parts.note: to steer is to navigate

explanation.surface: Sailing around the Americas aboard a vintage vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, now an old-fashioned vessel.
